key_insight: A manufactured automated X-ray inspection system combines modular mechanics and servo positioning to inspect pipe welds with ±1 mm positioning accuracy.
engineering_relevance: The design supports industrial weld inspection for pipes 40–508 mm in diameter and 6–12 m long, with internal or external inspection depending on diameter.
method: Use overhead-crane feeding and a rail-guided carrier to transport pipes to the X-ray positioning arm.
Align the weld using servo positioning, laser verification, an absolute encoder, and height adjustment; image at 25 cm intervals.
Verify structural performance through finite element analysis and experimental tests on the manufactured system.
evidence_signal: Structural analyses reported maximum stresses of 133.5 MPa for the arm and 211.1 MPa for the rail vehicle, with respective safety factors of 3.1 and 1.96; experimental validation was reported.
watch_item: The abstract does not quantify defect-detection performance, inspection throughput, or experimental agreement with structural simulations.
paper_title: Design and Validation of an Automated X-Ray Imaging System for Pipe Weld Inspection
